_about: The author shelves (2026-11-03, Adam: "Get me Tolkien and C. S. Lewis shelves and populate the coming titles with their public domain release dates. Also [Dorothy] Sayers and all of Chesterton"). Per author: what this repo fetches and builds (`standard_ebooks`, `archive_gutenberg`, read by fetch_sources.py and structure_texts.py, so the hosted Armarium builds them), what the house already held before (`held`), what is US public domain but not yet fetchable (`free_pending`, with why), and how many books wait for their day (`waiting`). The full list of every title with its US public-domain day is the house's public ledger, wordhoard apps/thewordhoard/data/author-shelves.json, and each waiting book is on the house release queue (apps/thewordhoard/data/release-queue.json); it is not copied here. RIGHTS: every book fetched here was first published in 1930 or before, so it is US public domain; Standard Ebooks' rights lines are read at fetch (fetch_sources.se_gate) and its production is CC0. Still-copyrighted books are never fetched or committed here: a locked copy, from a book the house owns, goes on the Armarium restricted shelf (ADR 0034) only. US status only: Tolkien (d. 1973), Lewis (d. 1963) and Sayers (d. 1957) are in copyright in life+70 countries.

free_pending.tolkien-poems-and-essays-in-periodicals-: Poems and essays in periodicals, 1915-1930 (1915): free as printed: Goblin Feet (Oxford Poetry 1915), his poems in A Northern Venture (Leeds, 1923), his 1920s articles in The Review of English Studies. Not gathered yet; each wants its printing found.
free_pending.tolkien-sir-gawain-and-the-green-knight-: Sir Gawain and the Green Knight (edited with E. V. Gordon) (1925): free in the US since 2021; the Middle English text with Tolkien and Gordon's notes and glossary. One open scan found (archive.org sirgawaingreenkn0000jrrt_m1f1, dated 1925); it needs its title page read and its OCR proofread, so it is not loaded yet. The 1967 second edition (revised by Norman Davis) is not free.

waiting.posthumous: Published after 1977 (Unfinished Tales, the Letters, Mr. Bliss, the twelve volumes of The History of Middle-earth, Roverandom and the rest): Tolkien's own words first printed between 1978 and 2002 open 1 January 2048; those first printed after 2002 (The Children of Húrin, The Fall of Arthur, his Beowulf translation, Beren and Lúthien, The Fall of Gondolin and the rest) open 1 January 2044, his life plus seventy years. Christopher Tolkien's editing (he died in 2020) runs to the end of 2090.

_excluded.pg48371: A Spring Harvest (1918) is G. B. Smith's poems; Tolkien only saw them into print with Christopher Wiseman. Not his book.

waiting.posthumous: The books gathered after his death (1936) mostly reprint newspaper essays: a piece first printed in 1930 or before is free already wherever it is found; the book that gathers it opens on its own day. Books gathered after 1977 (Daylight and Nightmare, the Ignatius Collected Works): words he saw printed before 1931 are free; others open 1 January 2048 (first printed 1978-2002) or are free now (first printed after 2002, his life plus seventy years having run out in 2006).
